summary: RFC 6513 describes using a partial mesh of multipoint-to-multipoint tunnels to carry bidirectional customer multicast in MPLS/BGP IP VPNs. This standards-track RFC specifies how to simulate that partial mesh using ingress replication, which lets a provider use that approach without needing multipoint-to-multipoint tunnel support in the network.

plainLanguage.summary: Instead of one shared delivery truck for everyone, the sender makes copies and sends a separate package to each receiver. It acts the same for the people getting the packages.

subtitle: Carrying bidirectional customer multicast over a provider network using ingress replication instead of MP2MP tunnels.

tldr.problem: Carrying bidirectional customer multicast through a provider core with a partial mesh of MP2MP tunnels needs signaling and state on the provider's P routers as well as on the PEs.
tldr.mechanism: The MP2MP tunnels are simulated by a mesh of P2MP tunnels built with Ingress Replication, driven by S-PMSI A-D routes and Leaf A-D routes that each PE advertises under defined rules.
tldr.outcome: A service provider can use Ingress Replication to offer transparent bidirectional multicast to VPN customers, with both the advantages and the disadvantages of Ingress Replication.

today: RFC 7740 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2016, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Problem and the Approach
sections.content:
Section 11.2 of RFC 6513 describes two methods of carrying Bidirectional PIM (BIDIR-PIM) customer traffic over a provider core without using the core as the Rendezvous Point Link or requiring Designated Forwarder election. All PEs of a VPN are split into partitions: each partition is the set of PEs that choose the same PE as Upstream PE with respect to the C-RPA, the Rendezvous Point Address in the customer's address space. A PE must discard bidirectional traffic from PEs outside its own partition.

RFC 7582 assumes an MP2MP P-tunnel is built with BIDIR-PIM (RFC 5015) or MP2MP mLDP (RFC 6388). Each needs signaling and state on P routers too. This document instead simulates the MP2MP tunnel with a mesh of P2MP tunnels, each instantiated by Ingress Replication. Because of that, the scheme inherits the advantages and the disadvantages of Ingress Replication in general.
sections.plainLanguage: The old way builds a special shared route through the whole network. The new way has each sender just make copies for the other members of its group, so the network in the middle needs no special setup.

sections.title: How It Differs from RFC 6514 Ingress Replication
sections.content:
The procedures here differ from those that set up the mesh of Ingress Replication tunnels in RFC 6514. Each PE on the MP2MP tunnel does not need to send a Selective P-Multicast Service Interface (S-PMSI) auto-discovery route (A-D route) for the P2MP tunnel it roots, and it does not need to send a Leaf A-D route to the root of every P2MP tunnel in the mesh.

Terminology comes from RFC 5015, RFC 6513, RFC 6514 and RFC 7582.
sections.plainLanguage: This works a little differently from the usual copy-and-send method, and it skips some of the announcements that method needs.

sections.title: Advertising S-PMSI A-D Routes
sections.content:
A PE (PEx) connected to a VPN site, whose next-hop interface toward some C-RPA is a VRF interface, MUST advertise a (C-*,C-*-BIDIR) S-PMSI A-D route, even if it has no local BIDIR-PIM join state for that C-RPA. It MAY also advertise (C-*,C-G-BIDIR) S-PMSI A-D routes when selective trees are needed for particular groups. The RFC suggests these could be triggered when the traffic rate goes above a threshold, which may require measuring both directions, and fan-out could also be considered.

These routes carry a PMSI Tunnel Attribute (PTA) with the tunnel type set to Ingress Replication, the Leaf Information Required flag set, a downstream-allocated MPLS label that other PEs in the same partition MUST use when sending relevant flows to this PE, and a Tunnel Identifier set to a routable address of the originator. Labels may be shared between P-tunnels.
sections.plainLanguage: Each member of the group announces: "I am here, and here is the special ticket number to put on packages for me."

sections.title: Responding with Leaf A-D Routes
sections.content:
When another PE (PEy) imports a (C-*,C-*-BIDIR) S-PMSI A-D route whose PTA specifies an Ingress Replication tunnel, has local BIDIR-PIM join state from its CEs, and chooses PEx as its Upstream PE for the C-RPA, PEy MUST advertise a Leaf A-D route. The same holds if it already imported the route and the join state arrives later. For (C-*,C-G-BIDIR) routes the rule is parallel.

The Leaf A-D route is encoded as in RFC 6514, except that its Route Targets equal those of the matching S-PMSI A-D route, so all VRFs importing that route import the Leaf A-D route too. The label in its PTA MUST be allocated specifically for PEx, so arriving traffic with that label can be tied to the partition PEx represents. This document also removes the RFC 6514 requirement that a PE take no action on a Leaf A-D route lacking an IP-address-specific Route Target, for these two route kinds.

To speed convergence, PEy MAY advertise a Leaf A-D route even if it does not choose PEx as Upstream PE. It then receives traffic from all PEs, and traffic with a label for a different choice is discarded.

PEy MUST withdraw the Leaf A-D route if the S-PMSI A-D route is withdrawn, if PEy no longer chooses PEx as Upstream PE (and only advertises in response to its Upstream PE), or if the relevant local join state is pruned.
sections.plainLanguage: When a member wants to join in, it replies with its own ticket number. The ticket tells the sender which group it belongs to, so packages from other groups get thrown away.

sections.title: Forwarding State
sections.content:
The forwarding rules match the "Match for Transmission" and "Match for Reception" rules of the "Flat Partitioning" method in RFC 7582, except that the (C-*,C-*) rules do not apply, since (C-*,C-*-BIDIR) S-PMSI A-D routes are always originated for a VPN supporting C-BIDIR flows.

If PEy itself advertises the S-PMSI A-D route and imports one from its Upstream PE, it keeps forwarding state whose Ingress Replication leaves are the originators of that route and of all relevant Leaf A-D routes, meaning those whose Route Key matches the Upstream PE's NLRI.

For "Sender Only Branches", where a router only sends upstream toward the C-RPA with no explicit join state, traffic must go to all PEs in the partition, not just the Upstream PE, because they may hold (C-*,C-G-BIDIR) joins that PEy does not know about. If there is also no (C-*,C-*-BIDIR) route from the Upstream PE, the tunnel has an empty set of leaves and PEy does not forward the traffic across the provider network.
sections.plainLanguage: A sender copies its package to every member it knows about. If it knows nobody, it sends nothing at all.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document raises no new security issues. Security considerations for the base protocol are covered in RFC 6513 and RFC 6514.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about here beyond what the earlier rules already cover.
